compact Escherichia colinucleoids retain characteristic shapes upon cell lysis in the presence of high concentrations of polylysine and are easily processed and visualized.

compact nucleoids can be released from E. coli in lysates containing polylysine and can be isolated and purified by a procedure that retains the characteristic shape of the nucleoids.

nucleoids released in the absence of spermidine and polylysine are not compact and that polylysine alone cannot prevent their decompaction upon lysis.

nucleoids can be released with their characteristic shapes in a form which is suitable for further processing.

nucleoid compaction is a property of DNA, not of DNA plus proteins, and that nucleoids can be released from cells in the absence of DNA binding proteins.
